investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-10-02T12:39:20–53Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api endpoint POST /api/agents could not reach the swarm gateway at the AWS ELB target (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents). Because the failure occurred before any agent was provisioned, all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is absent and no contract assertions could be evaluated.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed service at /v1/agents that the production-api proxies agent provisioning requests to — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check depends on a successful POST /api/agents call, which in turn requires the swarm gateway to be healthy. Because the gateway returned a connection error before any agent lifecycle data was produced, all three checks failed with the same message and zero evidence was collected. This is an infrastructure-layer failure localized to the swarm gateway / ELB target, not a failure of the eval runner logic or the expected-output contract definitions.

possibleCauses: Swarm gateway ELB target group is unhealthy or has no registered healthy instances in us-east-2, causing the production-api to receive a connection error when proxying to /v1/agents (strongest evidence: identical 502 across all three checks).
Swarm gateway service (the process behind the ELB) crashed, was restarted, or was temporarily scaled to zero at the time of the eval run, making the ELB return 502 for all inbound requests.

Network-level connectivity loss between the production-api layer and the swarm gateway ELB in us-east-2 (e.g., security group change, VPC routing issue, or AZ-level disruption) preventing TCP connections from being established.
Swarm gateway deployment or configuration change rendered the /v1/agents endpoint unavailable transiently (e.g., a rolling restart with no healthy instances during the window 12:39:20–12:39:53Z).

Eval runner authentication or routing misconfiguration causing the production-api to target a stale or incorrect ELB endpoint — less likely given the error message explicitly names the ELB URL and says 'error sending request', indicating a network-level failure rather than an auth rejection.

investigations.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-10-02T12:39:20–53Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api endpoint POST /api/agents could not reach the swarm gateway at the AWS ELB target (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents). Because the failure occurred before any agent was provisioned, all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is absent and no contract assertions could be evaluated.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed service at /v1/agents that the production-api proxies agent provisioning requests to — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check depends on a successful POST /api/agents call, which in turn requires the swarm gateway to be healthy. Because the gateway returned a connection error before any agent lifecycle data was produced, all three checks failed with the same message and zero evidence was collected. This is an infrastructure-layer failure localized to the swarm gateway / ELB target, not a failure of the eval runner logic or the expected-output contract definitions.

Network-level connectivity loss between the production-api layer and the swarm gateway ELB in us-east-2 (e.g., security group change, VPC routing issue, or AZ-level disruption) preventing TCP connections from being established.

investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check calls POST /api/agents as its first step (evidenced by createAgent at run-status-probes.mjs:1918), and all three checks received the same 502 bad_gateway response with error code "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning". Because no agent could be created, no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was ever collected, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely. This is an eval-infrastructure signal of a swarm gateway availability problem; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet to confirm a broader production outage.
